t: Up or down in normal pregnancy?
key: Ask what drives each value: hormonal vasodilation lowers resistance and pressure, volume expansion raises output and dilutes the blood, progesterone lowers carbon dioxide, and higher filtration lowers creatinine.
items: Expanded plasma volume raises preload and stroke volume, and heart rate climbs later, for a 40 to 50 percent rise.
Renin, angiotensin and aldosterone retain sodium and water, expanding plasma volume by about 40 to 50 percent.
Progesterone sensitizes the respiratory center to carbon dioxide, so each breath gets deeper while the rate barely changes.
Renal plasma flow rises early in pregnancy, lifting filtration by about half.
Estrogen drives the liver to make more fibrinogen and clotting factors, a hypercoagulable state that limits blood loss at delivery.
Estrogen raises thyroxine-binding globulin, so more T4 circulates bound while the free fraction stays normal.
Estrogen stimulates pituitary lactotrophs, which multiply and enlarge the gland as prolactin climbs toward term.
Progesterone, estrogen, relaxin and nitric oxide dilate arterioles, and the placenta adds a low-resistance circuit.
Blood pressure in the second trimester
Resistance falls more than output rises, so pressure reaches its nadir in the second trimester.
The uterus pushes the diaphragm up about 4 cm, shrinking the air left in the lungs at rest.
Ventilation outpaces carbon dioxide production, so PaCO2 falls to about 30 mm Hg.
The kidney excretes bicarbonate to compensate for the respiratory alkalosis, keeping pH only slightly alkaline.
Filtration rises about 50 percent, so creatinine falls to roughly 0.4 to 0.8 mg/dL.
Plasma expands more than red cell mass, so hemoglobin concentration falls even though red cells increase.
